This page is the help output of the `kode-gopher` binary built from the current sources. A test regenerates it and fails CI if it drifts.

Flags take one dash or two (`-namespace` and `--namespace` are the same).

## `kode-gopher`

```text
usage: kode-gopher <subcommand> [flags]

subcommands:
  exec <file.go>  ship a Go file into a sandbox and run it
  serve           start the MCP server (stdio, or streamable HTTP)
  auth <verb>     inspect ambient credentials (verb: status)
  version         print the build version
```

## `kode-gopher exec`

Runs one Go file in a sandbox and prints the outcome. Useful for checking a cluster setup without an MCP client; see [Getting started](/getting-started/sandbox-cluster/#check-it-from-the-command-line).

```text
usage: kode-gopher exec [flags] <file.go>

  -claim string
    	reattach to an existing sandbox claim instead of creating a new one
  -context string
    	kubeconfig context for the sandbox cluster (empty = the ambient current context)
  -credentials string
    	how the snippet gets Google credentials: forwarded (copy local ADC into the sandbox), access-token (mint a short-lived token from ADC and serve it to the run only), or service (the same, for --service-account, impersonated with ADC); access-token and service need --in-cluster (default "forwarded")
  -exec-timeout duration
    	per-phase sandbox /execute timeout (bounded upstream by PerAttemptTimeout, default 3min) (default 1m30s)
  -extra-imports string
    	comma-separated import paths to add as blank imports (forces go mod tidy to resolve them)
  -in-cluster
    	dial sandboxes by their in-cluster Service instead of port-forwarding (kode-gopher running in the cluster)
  -keep
    	leave the sandbox alive on exit (Disconnect) instead of deleting it (Close)
  -namespace string
    	Kubernetes namespace for the sandbox claim (must already exist) (default "default")
  -open-timeout duration
    	max time spent opening the sandbox (default 5m0s)
  -service-account string
    	--credentials=service: the Google service account snippets run as; kode-gopher's ADC needs roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on it
```

## `kode-gopher serve`

The MCP server. Over stdio for local use ([Getting started](/getting-started/connect/)), or streamable HTTP for a shared deployment ([Deploy for a team](/deploy/)).

```text
usage: kode-gopher serve [flags]

MCP server over stdio or streamable HTTP. Registers execute_go_code, gcp_auth_status and lookup_package_docs.

  -addr string
    	http: listen address (default ":8080")
  -auth string
    	http: static (one operator-issued bearer token) or oauth (kode-gopher's OAuth server fronting Google sign-in; snippets run as the signed-in user; needs --in-cluster) (default "static")
  -auth-token-file string
    	http, static auth: file holding the bearer token clients must send
  -auth-user string
    	http, static auth: the user the static token authenticates as (default "operator")
  -claim string
    	reattach to an existing sandbox claim instead of creating a new one on first tool call
  -claim-lease duration
    	http: sandbox claims expire this long after the last renewal, so a crashed server's sandboxes go away (default 10m0s)
  -context string
    	kubeconfig context for the sandbox cluster (empty = the ambient current context)
  -credentials string
    	how the snippet gets Google credentials: forwarded (copy local ADC into the sandbox), access-token (mint a short-lived token from ADC and serve it to the run only), or service (the same, for --service-account, impersonated with ADC); access-token and service need --in-cluster (default "forwarded")
  -exec-timeout duration
    	per-phase sandbox /execute timeout (bounded upstream by PerAttemptTimeout, default 3min) (default 1m30s)
  -in-cluster
    	dial sandboxes by their in-cluster Service instead of port-forwarding (kode-gopher running in the cluster)
  -max-sandboxes-per-user int
    	http: open sandboxes (MCP sessions with a sandbox) allowed per user; 0 = no cap (default 2)
  -namespace string
    	Kubernetes namespace for the sandbox claim (must already exist) (default "default")
  -oauth-allow-domains string
    	oauth: comma-separated Workspace domains (the ID token's hd claim) to admit
  -oauth-allow-groups string
    	oauth: comma-separated Google group emails to admit (nested membership counts; needs the Groups Reader admin role)
  -oauth-clients-file string
    	oauth: JSON array of pre-registered clients ({client_id, client_secret?, client_name, redirect_uris}, or {client_id, client_secret, service_account} for the client_credentials grant)
  -oauth-custody string
    	oauth: who holds users' Google grants: vault (Agent Identity credential vault) or sealed (inside kode-gopher's refresh token) (default "vault")
  -oauth-google-client-file string
    	oauth: kode-gopher's Google OAuth client, as the JSON the Cloud console downloads
  -oauth-issuer string
    	oauth: public base URL of this server, e.g. https://kg.example.com (the MCP endpoint is <issuer>/mcp)
  -oauth-keyring-file string
    	oauth: token-sealing keys, one "<id> <base64 32 bytes>" per line, sealing key first
  -oauth-open-registration
    	oauth: accept dynamically registered (DCR) and Client ID Metadata Document clients, not just pre-registered ones (default true)
  -oauth-vault-auth-provider string
    	oauth, vault custody: projects/<p>/locations/<l>/authProviders/<name>
  -open-timeout duration
    	max time spent opening the sandbox on first tool call (default 5m0s)
  -persistent
    	on shutdown, Disconnect from the sandbox (preserve for reattach) instead of Close (delete it)
  -project string
    	oauth: project reported to snippets as GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT
  -quota-project string
    	oauth: quota project reported to snippets as GOOGLE_CLOUD_QUOTA_PROJECT
  -service-account string
    	--credentials=service: the Google service account snippets run as; kode-gopher's ADC needs roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on it
  -session-timeout duration
    	http: end MCP sessions idle this long, closing their sandboxes (default 15m0s)
  -transport string
    	stdio, or http (streamable HTTP at <addr>/mcp, one sandbox per MCP session) (default "stdio")
```

## `kode-gopher auth`

```text
usage: kode-gopher auth <subcommand>

subcommands:
  status  print the credential identity kode-gopher will forward into sandboxes
```
